note: Track beat, step 6 (ladder clap-along:advanced): syncopation on the clap-along, the rhythm tool that marks each hit against the beat, in place of the strum-along that stood in for it. Only the &s first ("pattern": "offbeats"), then the push rhythm the level sets, then the push from memory over drums with the click to check. The old tempo ladder as a Stage selector is now moves (tempo), the later section keeping its distance, and the text counts the rhythm the way the tool writes it.

exercise.title: Syncopation: claps between the beats
exercise.why: A syncopated note lands between two beats, so you can only place it when something else, your foot, keeps marking the beats it avoids.

cells.text:
Press Start below. After a bar of count-in clicks, tap your foot on every click and tap Space on every note as it reaches the line: the four &s, halfway between two clicks.
Count "1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &" under your breath, and hit only on the "&".
If your hits slide onto the click, stop, keep your foot going, and come back in on the next bar.

Press Start below for a new rhythm: 1, the & of 2, the & of 3, and 4. The first and last hits land on a click, and the two in the middle fall between clicks. Keep your foot on every click.
Practice until the two middle hits feel as sure as the first one.

Press Play below to start the drums. Clap the same rhythm from memory, with your foot on the beat.
Then press Click below to switch the metronome on, and check that your first and last claps of the bar land on it.
{{?bpm}}At a faster tempo the rhythm keeps its shape: the middle two claps still fall halfway between clicks.
